name: Migrate users, spaces, folders, lists, custom fields and tasks from ClickUp to Asana

parameters.content:
## Migrate users, spaces, lists, custom fields and tasks from ClickUp to Asana

### How it works
1. The orchestrator checks your tokens and workspace IDs, then runs five stages in order: users, spaces, folders and lists, custom fields, tasks.
2. Each stage copies its objects to Asana and keeps a mapping in an n8n data table, so re-runs add no duplicates. Gmail messages report progress and failures.

### Setup
Copy each stage's nodes into its own workflow and save it. Every stage takes the same inputs: FeedbackEmail, ClickUpWorkspaceID, ClickUpPAK, ClickUpRateLimit (number), AsanaWorkspaceID, AsanaPAK, AsanaRateLimit (number). Stage 3 also needs AsanaPlan. Then pick one way to run:

**Manually, without the orchestrator**
1. In each stage, add a Manual Trigger and an Edit Fields node holding the inputs. Connect it to the stage's first Set Workflow Environment node (stage 5: replace its trigger).
2. Fill in the values and run stages 1 to 5 in order.

**With the orchestrator**
1. Add an Execute Workflow Trigger with the inputs as the first node of stages 1 to 4 (stage 5 has one).
2. Fill in Set Initial Workflow Environment. In each Call node, select that stage's workflow and map every input to the field of the same name in Set Workflow Environment (orchestrator).
3. Run the orchestrator.

**Values you need:** an email for status messages, a ClickUp token and workspace ID, an Asana token and workspace ID, and your Asana plan name. Rate limits per minute: ClickUp 100 (Business Plus 1000, Enterprise 10000); Asana 150 on Personal, else 1500. The orchestrator works these out; manually, enter them.

assignments.name: ClickUpRateLimit
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const p = ($('Check ClickUp Workspace ID').first().json.plan_name || '').toLowerCase(); return p.includes('enterprise') ? 10000 : p.includes('business plus') ? 1000 : 100; })() }}

parameters.message:
=

Hi,

Your ClickUp to Asana migration has not started, because Asana did not accept the personal access token entered in the workflow settings. Nothing has been changed in either account.

To fix it

  1. Open the Asana developer console.
  2. Create a new personal access token and copy it straight away. Asana shows it only once.
  3. Correct the token in Set Initial Workflow Environment, without spaces, and run the workflow again.
parameters.subject: ClickUp to Asana migration: Asana token not accepted

parameters.message:
=

Hi,

Your Asana token is valid, but the workspace ID you entered ({{ String($('Set Initial Workflow Environment').first().json.AsanaWorkspaceID ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}) was not found, or cannot be accessed with that token. Nothing has been changed in either account.

To fix it

  1. Sign in to Asana in your browser. Your workspace ID is the first number after app.asana.com/1/ in the address bar.
  2. If your address looks different, open this page and copy the gid of the workspace you are migrating into.
  3. Make sure the token belongs to a member of that workspace.
  4. Correct the value in Set Initial Workflow Environment and run the workflow again.
parameters.subject: ClickUp to Asana migration: Asana workspace ID not found

parameters.message:
=

Hi,

Your Asana details were accepted, but ClickUp did not accept the personal API token entered in the workflow settings. Nothing has been changed in either account.

To fix it

  1. In ClickUp, click your avatar, then Settings, then Apps.
  2. Under API Token, generate or copy your token. It starts with pk_.
  3. Correct that token in Set Initial Workflow Environment and run the workflow again.
parameters.subject: ClickUp to Asana migration: ClickUp token not accepted

Hi,

Your Asana details and ClickUp token were accepted, but the ClickUp workspace ID you entered ({{ String($('Set Initial Workflow Environment').first().json.ClickUpWorkspaceID ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}) was not found, or cannot be accessed with that token. Nothing has been changed in either account.

To fix it

  1. Open ClickUp in your browser. The workspace ID is the number right after app.clickup.com/ in the address bar.
  2. Use a token from a workspace Owner or Admin, because the migration reads users and spaces.
  3. Correct the value in Set Initial Workflow Environment and run the workflow again.

parameters.message:
=

Hi,

Your credentials were accepted and the migration is now running.

Connected accounts

  • ClickUp: {{ String($('Check ClickUp Credentials').first().json.user.username ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }} (workspace {{ String($('Set Initial Workflow Environment').first().json.ClickUpWorkspaceID ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}, plan: {{ String($('Check ClickUp Workspace ID').first().json.plan_name ?? 'not reported').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }})
  • Asana: {{ String($('Check Asana Credentials').first().json.data.name ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }} (workspace: {{ String($('Check Asana Workspace ID').first().json.data.name ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}, plan: {{ String($json.AsanaPlan ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }})

Your ClickUp plan allows {{ String($('Set Workflow Environment (orchestrator)').first().json.ClickUpRateLimit ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }} requests per minute and your Asana plan allows {{ String($json.AsanaRateLimit ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}. The migration paces itself to stay under these limits.

What will be migrated, in this order

  1. Users
  2. Spaces
  3. Folders and lists
  4. Custom fields
  5. Tasks, with their subtasks, comments, checklists and attachments

Depending on the number of tasks, this can take from several minutes to several hours. You will receive an email after each step and again when everything is done. Please do not revoke either token until you receive the completion email.
parameters.subject: ClickUp to Asana migration: started

parameters.message:
=

Hi,

Your ClickUp to Asana migration has finished. Users, spaces, lists, custom fields and tasks, with their subtasks, comments, checklists and attachments, have been migrated from ClickUp workspace {{ String($('Set Workflow Environment (orchestrator)').first().json.ClickUpWorkspaceID ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }} into your Asana workspace “{{ String($('Check Asana Workspace ID').first().json.data.name ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}”.

Your mapping files

Four CSV files are attached. They match every ClickUp item to its new Asana item: spaces to teams, lists to projects, custom fields, and tasks. Please save them now, because they are the only copy.

Your data and your keys

Please revoke both tokens now:

  • ClickUp: Settings, Apps, API Token, Regenerate
  • Asana: open the developer console and delete the token you created

Next steps

Open Asana and check your projects. If something looks wrong or missing, check the n8n execution history. Please do not run the migration a second time on the same workspace, because that creates duplicates.

## 1. Enter your settings
The manual trigger starts the run. Fill in the Set Initial Workflow Environment node: your email, tokens, workspace IDs and Asana plan.

nodes.name: Section - Check tokens and workspace IDs (orchestrator)

parameters.content:
## 2. Check tokens and workspace IDs
Each token and workspace ID is tested against Asana and ClickUp. A wrong value sends an email that explains the fix, and the run stops.

## 3. Start the run
The settings for the stages are prepared (rate limits, table names), and a start email is sent.

## 4. Run the five stages
Each stage is its own workflow. They run in order, and each one emails its progress and a mapping CSV.

## 5. Build the mapping files
Read the four mapping tables, convert them to CSV files, and email them with the final summary.

## 6. Clean up
Delete the four temporary mapping tables.

parameters.message:
=

Hi,

The migration has stopped because the workflow could not add the ClickUp user “{{ String(($('Loop Over Users').item.json.UserName) ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}” ({{ String(($('Loop Over Users').item.json.Email) ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}) to Asana.

Error: {{ String(($json.error?.message || $json.message || 'Unknown error') ?? '').replace(/[&<]/g, c => c == '&' ? '&' : '<') }}

Common causes

  • Your Asana token does not have workspace admin permission to invite members
  • Your Asana workspace has reached its paid seat limit
  • The email address is invalid
  • Asana was rate limiting requests (safe to retry)
  • A temporary network problem

What to do

Fix the issue, then run the workflow again. Users already added are skipped, so nothing is duplicated.

Your temporary migration data will be deleted automatically within 3 days. If you decide not to retry, please revoke your ClickUp and Asana tokens.

## 2. Find users that are missing in Asana
Read the users of both tools, clean the email addresses, and keep only the ClickUp users that are not in Asana yet.

## 3. Add the missing users
Each missing user is invited to the Asana workspace, then the name is updated. A failed invite goes to the error email.

When all users are processed, a short progress email goes to the user.

## 5. Report an error
An email explains the cause and the run stops.

parameters.content:
## 2. Prepare the mapping table
Look for the task mapping table and create it if it does not exist yet. A repeated run reads the rows already saved.

## 3. Read the ClickUp tasks
Read all spaces, folders and lists, then their tasks and subtasks. Keep the tasks that are not migrated yet, parents first.

## 4. Create the Asana tasks
Create each task in its project and section. A subtask is created under its parent task.

## 5. Copy custom field values
Convert each ClickUp field value to the matching Asana field, and write all values to the task in one call.

## 6. Copy the priority
The ClickUp priority is set on the Asana task.

## 7. Copy comments
The comments of the ClickUp task are added to the Asana task.

## 8. Copy checklists
Each checklist item becomes a subtask of the Asana task.

## 9. Copy attachments
Each attachment is downloaded from ClickUp and uploaded to the Asana task.

## 10. Save the task mapping
The new Asana task is stored next to the ClickUp task in the mapping table.

## 1. Receive the settings
The Orchestrator passes the tokens, workspace IDs and rate limits. They are copied into one set of fields that every later node reads.

## 11. Send the mapping file
The mapping table becomes a CSV file and is emailed to the user.

# Orchestrator
Start here to run all five stages in order. Fill in Set Initial Workflow Environment, select each stage's workflow in the five Call nodes and map their inputs (see the overview).

# Stage 1 of 5: Users
Adds ClickUp users to Asana. Copy this stage into its own workflow and add an Execute Workflow Trigger first (see the overview). Run it alone, or call it from the orchestrator.

# Stage 2 of 5: Spaces
Creates an Asana team for each ClickUp space. Copy this stage into its own workflow and add an Execute Workflow Trigger first (see the overview). Run it alone, or call it from the orchestrator.

# Stage 3 of 5: Folders and lists
Creates Asana portfolios and projects from ClickUp folders and lists. Copy this stage into its own workflow and add an Execute Workflow Trigger first (see the overview). Run it alone, or call it from the orchestrator.

# Stage 4 of 5: Custom fields
Creates Asana custom fields and adds them to projects. Copy this stage into its own workflow and add an Execute Workflow Trigger first (see the overview). Run it alone, or call it from the orchestrator.

# Stage 5 of 5: Tasks
Copies ClickUp tasks, fields, comments, checklists and attachments to Asana. This stage already has its own trigger. Run it alone, or call it from the orchestrator.
